editorial.verdict: A 1,500 spm straight-stitch quilting machine with no published throat figure, so check the reach before you pay.
editorial.whoFor: Quilters and straight-stitch sewists who want a 1,500 spm straight-stitch head with a thread trimmer and knee lifter, and are happy with foot-control speed.
editorial.skipIf: You need any stitch but straight, you want a published throat figure, or you want the front speed control and sub-tension dial owners credit to the TL-2010Q.

Juki lists a knee lifter at 12 mm and an auxiliary table in the box, and owners praise the extension table.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Juki TL-2000Qi?
faqs.a: Owners mostly praise the speed, the power through heavy fabric and a roomy throat, and many call it quiet for a fast machine. The repeated complaints are the automatic needle threader (11 of the 15 voices who mention threading are negative), the free motion foot not being in the box, and the pedal trimmer cutting thread by accident. The read covers 109 first-hand voices from 47 Reddit threads and 2 retailer pages, 2011 to 2026, and Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the TL-2000Qi and the TL-2010Q?
faqs.a: Owners repeatedly say the TL-2010Q's main addition is a speed control, and some add a sub-tension (pretension) dial. Juki's TL-2000Qi page lists microcomputer speed control with foot control only and no slider, while the sub-tension dial is not confirmed by a Juki document for the 2000Qi [verify]. Juki lists $2,169 for the TL-2010Q and $1,799 for the TL-2000Qi, and owners put the gap at $200 to $300 at a local dealer.

faqs.q: What is the price of the Juki TL-2000Qi?
faqs.a: Juki lists a suggested retail of $1,799 and tells buyers to contact an authorized dealer. Amazon showed $899 on 2026-10-01, so most buyers pay far less than list. Prices drift weekly, so use the price band on this page as the stable guide.

faqs.q: How big is the throat on the Juki TL-2000Qi?
faqs.a: Juki does not publish a throat, arm or needle-to-arm figure for this model. Its page says Mid-Arm and a work area up to 23 in with the auxiliary table. Dealers quote 9 in, but that has no Juki source, so we show the throat as [verify]; one owner finds it narrower than expected, and others quilted a king size quilt on it.

faqs.q: Is the Juki TL-2000Qi a long-arm machine?
faqs.a: No. Juki calls it Mid-Arm. A dealer listing title says Long-Arm, which is a retailer label, not a measurement, and the 23 in figure is the work area with the auxiliary table attached.

faqs.q: Where can I find the Juki TL-2000Qi manual?
faqs.a: Juki publishes a 40-page instruction manual PDF for the TL-2000Qi on its product page, with the specification table on page 12, and a two-page catalog. Juki's own documents disagree on some figures, such as the auxiliary table depth, 355 mm on the product page and 277 mm in the manual.

faqs.q: How do you thread the Juki TL-2000Qi, and does the needle threader work?
faqs.a: Juki lists a push-lever automatic needle threader. Owners are not fond of it: 11 of the 15 voices who mention threading are negative, and one says it never works, even after a dealer needed four tries. Many owners skip it and thread the needle by hand.

faqs.q: Can the Juki TL-2000Qi do free motion quilting?
faqs.a: Juki's page claims 'Nothing Free Motion Quilts Better than a Juki', which is a maker claim. Juki's list of what is in the box has no free motion foot, and 5 of the 7 owners who mention free motion report the foot is not included and must be bought separately. Others report no tension problems in free motion quilting.

faqs.q: Does the Juki TL-2000Qi have a speed control slider?
faqs.a: No front slider is listed. Juki's page describes microcomputer-based speed control with foot control only, and owners say the TL-2010Q is the model with the speed control. Some owners ask how to sew slower on pedal control alone.
